red_tests.failure_fingerprint: 4 failed, 6 passed; KAN272_COLD_START: a backend timeout and an upstream 5xx both collapse into the single backend_unreachable 502, so a transient cold start is indistinguishable from a real outage; failure responses carry no Cache-Control: no-store; there is no dedicated shorter liveness timeout
1 failed, 9 passed; the superseded KAN-271 assertion still requires a 502 for an upstream 5xx

rationale: Freeze the KAN-272 cold-start contract before source work. Render's free plan spins down after ~15 minutes idle and takes ~50 seconds to wake, while the Worker proxy timeout is 15000 ms - a ~35 s gap, so the first request after an idle period could never succeed and the caller simply hung until the abort fired. Keep-alive was evaluated and rejected: holding one free Render service warm 24/7 consumes roughly 730 of the 750 free instance-hours per calendar month, leaving no headroom, and it holds only while this is the sole service in the workspace; the existing cron is 6-hourly and cannot be relied on for warmth. Upgrading the plan is a paid change requiring explicit owner sign-off and is ruled out by the standing free-only constraint, so it was not selected. The chosen mitigation is to make the failure useful and honest rather than to lengthen the wait: distinguish a transient cold start (503 + code backend_waking + Retry-After) from a genuine outage (502 + code backend_unreachable + Retry-After), give liveness endpoints a shorter dedicated timeout so they answer fast, and mark failure responses Cache-Control: no-store so a transient error is never cached. Tests drive the real worker module with a stubbed global fetch, simulating an AbortError for the timeout path, so a change that merely renames a status cannot pass.
